# massdriver_organization_settings (Resource)

Organization-wide settings for the provider's configured organization. Declare at most one. Only the arguments you set are managed: an omitted argument keeps whatever value the organization already has. Destroying this resource stops managing the settings without changing them. Requires the `organization:manageSettings` action (organization admins).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "massdriver_organization_settings" "this" {
  grant_new_bundles_to_all_projects = true

  naming_convention = "{{attrs.team}}-{{instance.id}}"

  default_tags = [
    massdriver_custom_attribute.team.key,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `default_tags` (Set of String) Custom attribute keys whose values are sent to deployments as default cloud tags. Each key must apply to instances. `managed-by` and `md-instance` are always sent. Set to `[]` to send only those. Once an organization has chosen its default tags it cannot return to the legacy tag set, so removing this argument leaves the current tags in place.
- `grant_new_bundles_to_all_projects` (Boolean) When `true`, each new bundle repository is automatically granted `repo:pull` to every project; when `false`, new repositories stay restricted until a grant is authored. Only affects repositories created after the change.
- `naming_convention` (String) Liquid template that names every provisioned cloud resource, e.g. `{{attrs.team}}-{{instance.id}}`. Atoms include `{{org.id}}`, `{{project.id}}`, `{{environment.id}}`, `{{instance.id}}`, `{{component.suffix}}`, and `{{attrs.KEY}}` for any declared custom attribute. Set to `""` to restore the default `{{instance.id}}-{{component.suffix}}`. The resolved name is fixed on each instance when it is first created; changing the convention does not rename existing instances.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import massdriver_organization_settings.this <organization_id>
```
